account:
It is noon on day 1, and I am home for my scheduled lunch. Town life appears largely routine. I attended the ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill; no worker provided a substantive report, but I saw 82 hay bales in the mill's sales chest. That establishes stock present there, not the condition of all town grain supplies.

The unusual matter is a persistent, vague rumour of a bridge or port change associated with the bakery. Several townsfolk repeated it, and one said the baker and freight had been there. I have heard no actual proposal, details, or firsthand account establishing what change is intended. Repetition may simply be the same rumour circulating; I cannot infer a plan or its purpose from it.

The secretary has found no proposal, accounts ledger, or correspondence location in the office records checked. The treasury contained emeralds but no ledger or letters. I authorized further enquiries among town hall staff, with a report expected at thirteen hundred, when I attend council letters. These missing records remain an administrative question, not evidence of wrongdoing.

Today's confirmed special event is the eighteen hundred community gathering with the innkeeper in the great hall. Freight offered an escort from my office, which I approved; the secretary is confirming it. I know of no established connection between that gathering and the bakery rumour. My remaining appointments include office business at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, the gathering at eighteen, and home at nineteen.
